lines.trans: Hello, Andrey Nikolaevich, I have heard very much about you.

words.gram: male given name, used as address

lines.trans: Probably you have also heard a lot about me today.
Katya works as a chef right here in our restaurant.
In the kitchen she is in charge of molecular cuisine.
And she has a very big future ahead of her.
Mom, do not exaggerate, I am just an ordinary chef.
Forgive me, Katya, I behaved very foolishly.
And understand me too, I panicked a bit today.
After all, you are the first girl Nikita has introduced me to.
I could not even imagine that everything was so serious.
Forgive me once again and all the best to you!

познакомиться.gloss: to get acquainted, to meet (for the first time)

meanings.en: to meet for the first time, to get acquainted
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'знакомиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get acquainted, to meet (for the first time)', paired with 'знакомиться'.

examples.text: Папа, добрый день, я хочу тебя познакомить.
examples.trans: Dad, good afternoon, I want to introduce you.

examples.text: Мечтала познакомиться с твоими друзьями.
examples.trans: I dreamed of meeting your friends.

examples.text: Где вы познакомились?
examples.trans: Where did you meet?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.text: Поэтому извините меня, пожалуйста, мне надо идти работать.
examples.trans: So excuse me, please, I have to go work.

examples.trans: Forgive me, Katya, I behaved very foolishly.

examples.text: Ещё раз простите меня и всего вам доброго!
examples.trans: Forgive me once again and all the best to you!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'led, behaved', paired with 'повести'.

examples.text: Тебе нужна невеста, равная нам по статусу.
examples.trans: You need a bride equal to us in status.

examples.text: Твоя ровесница, наверняка девушка с хорошим образованием.
examples.trans: Your peer, surely a girl with a good education.

examples.text: Я обещаю вести себя крайне аккуратно.
examples.trans: I promise to behave extremely neatly.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'themselves', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Просто она ведёт себя так, будто мы встречаемся.
examples.trans: She just acts as if we are dating.

examples.text: Как ты себя чувствуешь, мой бедный защитник?
examples.trans: How do you feel, my poor defender?

examples.text: Ну как ты себя чувствуешь, наш смелый боец?
examples.trans: Well how are you feeling, our brave fighter?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Раз она ради тебя такие глупости устраивает.
examples.trans: Since she is staging such foolishness for your sake.

examples.text: Простите меня, Катя, я вёл себя очень глупо.
examples.trans: Forgive me, Katya, I behaved very foolishly.

examples.text: Это глупо.
examples.trans: That's stupid.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.text: Я всё понял, сразу говорю, денег не дам.
examples.trans: I understood everything, I am telling you right away, I will not give you money.

examples.text: Я не понял.
examples.trans: I didn't understand.

examples.text: Со всеми поделись поровну, понял?
examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: И если честно, меня это немного напрягает.
examples.trans: And to be honest, that stresses me out a bit.

examples.text: Подожди немного, сейчас ты сама всё узнаешь.
examples.trans: Wait a little, right now you will find out everything yourself.

examples.text: Лена, я просто хочу немного брата разыграть.
examples.trans: Lena, I just want to play a little prank on my brother.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'паниковать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'panicked'.

examples.text: И вы меня поймите, я сегодня немного запаниковал.
examples.trans: And understand me too, I panicked a bit today.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и запаниковать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and panicked on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это хорошо, ведь мне он ничего не рассказывает.
examples.trans: That is good, because he tells me nothing at all.

examples.text: Просто она ведёт себя так, будто мы встречаемся.
examples.trans: She just acts as if we are dating.

examples.text: Ей сейчас тяжело, ведь она с парнем рассталась.
examples.trans: It is hard for her right now, because she broke up with her boyfriend.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('first').

examples.text: Я просто первую машину на улице поймал.
examples.trans: I just flagged down the first car on the street.

examples.text: Ведь вы первая девушка, с которой меня знакомит Никита.
examples.trans: After all, you are the first girl Nikita has introduced me to.

examples.text: Это мой первый день.
examples.trans: This is my first day.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'miss' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Познакомься, пожалуйста, это Катя, моя любимая девушка!
examples.trans: Meet her, please, this is Katya, my beloved girlfriend!

examples.text: Папа, познакомься, это моя девушка.
examples.trans: Dad, meet her, this is my girlfriend.

examples.text: Он назвал меня своей девушкой, это меня напрягает.
examples.trans: He called me his girlfriend, that stresses me out.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Там сейчас свежее мясо должны привезти, проконтролируй.
examples.trans: They are supposed to deliver fresh meat there right now, go check it.

examples.text: Сеня, вчера вечеринка у тебя получилась отличная.
examples.trans: Senya, your party yesterday turned out great.

examples.text: Денис, расскажи, как у тебя со Светой?
examples.trans: Denis, tell me, how are things with you and Sveta?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who, which (relative)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Наверняка найдётся парень, который будет вами гордиться.
examples.trans: Surely a guy will be found who will be proud of you.

examples.text: Ведь вы первая девушка, с которой меня знакомит Никита.
examples.trans: After all, you are the first girl Nikita has introduced me to.

examples.text: Это мэр, который держит слово.
examples.trans: This is a mayor who keeps his word.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'introduces'.

examples.text: Папа, добрый день, я хочу тебя познакомить.
examples.trans: Dad, good afternoon, I want to introduce you.

examples.text: Ведь вы первая девушка, с которой меня знакомит Никита.
examples.trans: After all, you are the first girl Nikita has introduced me to.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'even', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Но я думаю, это даже к лучшему.
examples.trans: But I think that is even for the best.

examples.text: И с тех пор даже учителя называли его Зюзей.
examples.trans: And since then even the teachers called him Zyuzya.

examples.text: Представляешь, от волнения я даже счёт забыл принести.
examples.trans: Can you imagine, from nerves I even forgot to bring the bill.

meanings.en: to think it over, to give it a thought
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think (it over)', paired with 'думать'.

examples.text: И подумает, что я снова к тебе пристаю!
examples.trans: And thinks that I am hitting on you again!

examples.text: Я даже подумать не мог, что всё так серьёзно.
examples.trans: I could not even imagine that everything was so serious.

examples.text: Я подумаю.
examples.trans: I'll think about it.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Я главный управляющий, чем я могу вам помочь?
examples.trans: I am the general manager, how can I help you?

examples.text: Сегодня не могу.
examples.trans: I can't today.

examples.text: Этого не может быть.
examples.trans: That can't be.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никак, это было просто чтобы Катя поревновала.
examples.trans: Nothing at all, that was just to make Katya jealous.

examples.text: Слушай, а Света знает, что у вас ничего нет?
examples.trans: Listen, does Sveta know that there is nothing between you two?

examples.text: Потому что он уже давно сидит здесь.
examples.trans: Because he has been sitting here for a long time already.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Всё, Миша, пока, не звони мне больше.
examples.trans: That is it, Misha, bye, do not call me anymore.

examples.text: Я всё понял, сразу говорю, денег не дам.
examples.trans: I understood everything, I am telling you right away, I will not give you money.

examples.text: Витя, в Америке у меня всё отлично работает.
examples.trans: Vitya, in America everything works great for me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Так на чём мы с тобой остановились?
examples.trans: So where did you and I leave off?

examples.text: Я тебя понимаю, у меня дочь такого же возраста.
examples.trans: I understand you, I have a daughter of the same age.

examples.text: А чего ты тут так громко кричишь?
examples.trans: Why are you shouting so loudly in here?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ерьёзно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Всё, успокоились, я тебя серьёзно предупредил.
examples.trans: Alright, we calmed down, I gave you a serious warning.

examples.text: Это серьёзный человек, не втягивай его в авантюры!
examples.trans: He is a serious person, do not drag him into risky ventures!

examples.text: Нет, Катя, это просто серьёзное предупреждение.
examples.trans: No, Katya, this is simply a serious warning.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Эта смешная история пошла ещё со школы.
examples.trans: This funny story started back in school.

examples.text: Я не хочу делать ей ещё больнее.
examples.trans: I do not want to make her hurt even more.

examples.text: Представляешь, за меня ещё никогда никто не дрался!
examples.trans: Can you imagine, nobody has ever fought over me before!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'time, occasion' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я всё понял, сразу говорю, денег не дам.
examples.trans: I understood everything, I am telling you right away, I will not give you money.

examples.text: Подожди, на этот раз это реально работает!
examples.trans: Wait, this time it really works!

examples.text: Скажи, что ты придумал на этот раз?
examples.trans: Tell me, what did you come up with this time?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: А вы чего смеётесь, быстро все за работу!
examples.trans: What are you laughing at, everyone get to work quickly!

examples.text: Быстро идите все на свои места!
examples.trans: Everyone go to your stations quickly!

examples.text: И он совсем не хочет меня там слушать.
examples.trans: And he does not want to listen to me there at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'брый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good').

examples.text: Доброе утро, твой человек надёжный, но очень медленный.
examples.trans: Good morning, your contact is reliable, but very slow.

examples.text: Добро пожаловать в наш ресторан, дорогой гость!
examples.trans: Welcome to our restaurant, dear guest!

examples.text: Папа, добрый день, я хочу тебя познакомить.
examples.trans: Dad, good afternoon, I want to introduce you.
